body:
Watch the BJP supporter at the CJP protest.

1. His son studied 12 hours a day for two years.
2. He and his brother-in-law took loans and mortgaged their land to fund it.
3. Then the NEET paper leaked. He says it plainly: this didn't destroy his kid's future, it destroyed their future.
4. He's a Sanghi. He'll probably still vote for Modi. But even he is now saying it out loud, "BJP leaders send their kids abroad while we suffer," and demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

That's the whole point.

The hardcore Sanghi voter won't move. Nothing shifts them. But this man isn't the target.

The target is the huge silent crowd watching him, the fence-sitters who can be persuaded.

When they see even BJP's own people hurting, one thought lands: if the party does this to its own loyalists, what will it do to us?

And here's what people forget.

In 2024, BJP's vote share fell by just 0.77%.

That tiny drop took them from 303 seats to 240. In our electoral system, a small shift in votes becomes a huge shift in seats.

Now add the rest: no jobs, rising prices, economic misery, one leaked exam after another. Anger like that doesn't stay quiet. It spreads.

CJP's strength is that it belongs to no party. That's exactly why it works.

A disenchanted BJP voter listens to another disenchanted BJP voter, but would not talk to me, you, or even Congress. Because that's how much India has changed.

CJP can do what no party can: stoke the disappointment, start the anger.

But anger needs somewhere to go. Fire needs a path. CJP can light it, but someone still has to be the destination that turns that anger into votes.

So the job is simple. Let the CJP light the fire. And Congress should build the channel to carry it. That's how 240 becomes less than 150.

This is purely electoral math, votes and seats, not about me. Criticise me all you want; the numbers stay the same.

Thousands of participants from across India have gathered at Savitribai Phule Pune University in Pune for a massive protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Abhijeet Dipke. The nationwide agitation targets repeated irregularities in CBSE and NEET examinations, with CJP demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak and CBSE OSM exam evaluation controversy. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and hundreds of students are among those expected to participate. The protest, beginning at 4 PM on the SPPU campus, will later expand to major cities including Lucknow, Amritsar, Bengaluru, Jaipur, and Hyderabad. From June 20, an indefinite sit-in protest will be held at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi until Pradhan steps down.

body:
These CJP protesters have no clue who or what they’re actually backing - and that’s exactly the point.

Take the viral clip of that protester (Ujjwal) from the Jantar Mantar event. He joins a protest demanding the Education Minister’s resignation over NEET leaks and exam scams, but when asked point-blank about Umar Khalid, he blanks out or dodges. Classic example.

Most rank-and-file “cockroaches” are just frustrated Gen-Z kids angry about real issues - paper leaks, unemployment, broken education system. Fair enough. But they’re being herded into a movement whose core leadership has a documented history of aligning with figures and narratives widely seen as anti-national.

The leadership angle:

•  Founder Abhijeet Dipke (the guy who started it all as “satire”): Former AAP social media/comms volunteer. Old posts and statements show him defending or supporting Umar Khalid (the same activist accused in the Delhi riots conspiracy case under UAPA). Critics like Arnab Goswami have grilled him directly on AAP links, “tukde-tukde” narratives, and apparent support for controversial separatist-leaning voices. The protest timing even overlapped with Umar Khalid-related developments, and some CJP events/chants reportedly shifted from “NEET accountability” to “Umar Khalid is our leader” vibes.

•  Official spokespersons:

•  Saurav Das (chief spokesperson): Investigative journalist with a track record of sharp attacks on the judiciary and cases tied to AAP figures.

•  Vijeta Dahiya: Political researcher/filmmaker/content creator closely associated with Dhruv Rathee’s circle (known for heavy anti-government content).

•  Ashutosh Ranka: IIT-LSE background, with past AAP-adjacent connections reported in some circles.

This isn’t some organic, leaderless youth uprising. It’s a movement started by someone with clear past ties to AAP (a party often accused by nationalists of soft-pedaling on national security issues) and spokespeople from the same ideological ecosystem.

The real agenda claim:

Critics say it’s not about fixing exams — it’s about manufacturing chaos and riots under the cover of “youth anger.”

•  Genuine student frustration gets hijacked.

•  Protests that start on education quickly get polluted with slogans for jailed activists like Umar Khalid.

•  The “cockroach” branding and calls for “ruckus” (in some old videos) get framed as resilience, but opponents call it deliberate destabilization — especially with the founder operating partly from the US while pushing street action in India.

In the last five months, three major protests have taken place against the Education Ministry:

▪️GC protest against the UGC Act
▪️NSUI protest against the NEET paper leak
▪️Cockroach protest against the NEET paper leak

Surprisingly, despite being backed by significant financial resources (Cockroach Party) and strong organisational strength (NSUI), both CJP and NSUI failed to achieve their objectives. In contrast, the GC group, a relatively small network of online protesters, succeeded in drawing institutional attention, securing a stay order from the Supreme Court, and forcing the government to backtrack.

This outcome is precisely why OSINT researchers like me got curious to examine what enabled the GC group to succeed where the Cockroach and NSUI efforts fell short.

Key reasons behind the GC group’s success:

1. Solution-centric approach: The GC group focused on solutions. They carefully analysed the process, identified critical flaws, and targeted them directly. In contrast, CJP and NSUI did not appear serious about delivering solutions. They seemed more invested in political point-scoring, which made their approach lack sincerity and credibility.

2. Constitutional methods + powerful messaging: The GC group chose the constitutional route by filing a petition in the Supreme Court. They complemented this with clear, compelling social media messaging that cut through the noise and even drew support from pro-BJP handles.

On the other side, NSUI failed to generate any meaningful social media buzz. CJP created some noise, but it lacked focus, clarity, and impact. Their reliance on street protests without a sharp narrative ultimately limited their effectiveness.

GC group kept their movement non-political and didnt carry any political baggage while NUSI protest was completely political and CJP tried to show them non-political but exposed badly in this

The GC group’s success, set against the failures of CJP and NSUI, offers a clear case study in how to achieve tangible results in today’s environment.

Key takeaways:
1. Solution focus beats political theatre
2. Constitutional + digital hybrid outperforms street activism
3. Authentic non-partisan positioning is a force multiplier
4. Strategy and narrative discipline is more powerful than money and organisation

Paper Leaks Problem - What to do

1. Map out the full process
Break down the issue end-to-end to understand exactly how it functions.

2. Identify the bottlenecks
Pinpoint the specific flaws, gaps, or points of failure in the system.

3. Offer a robust solution
Present a clear, practical, and well-reasoned alternative instead of mere criticism.

4. Create focused social media buzz
Build strong narrative momentum around your solution with sharp, solution-oriented messaging.

5. Engage the government constructively
Treat the government as a partner, not an enemy. They too want improvement and will respond positively to sincere, well-presented solutions.

6. Approach the courts if required
If the government fails to act, escalate through constitutional means by filing a petition in the appropriate court.

" Lo ji ho gya protest " 🤡💀

Is the Cockroach Janata Party trying to end this protest right now?

The CJP protest, which has been going on at Jantar Mantar, Delhi since June 20th, has not yet generated the kind of movement Abhijeet Dipke was expecting.

By putting Sonam Wangchuk on a hunger strike, abhijeet_dipke must have thought that raising the issue of Dharmendra Pradhan and the NEET paper leak would be beneficial for them. But the results were the opposite. While the CJP was targeting and provoking the Delhi Police every day, the Delhi Police allowed them to protest without permission. Left-wing students’ organisation All India Students’ Association (AISA) recently announced a week-long nationwide campaign ‘Cockroaches on the streets’, across Delhi, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The campaign began yesterday (11th June) and will continue till 18th June. Yesterday, AISA members wearing cockroach masks protested in Delhi University’s North Campus, Kamla Nagar, Patel Chest, Gurmandi and Vijaynagar.

This comes days after the Left-wing students’ organisation joined the farcical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest held at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on 6th June. The protest was organised in the name of demanding the resignation of the Union Education Minister for the recent NEET exam paper leak and raising issues related to students. However, the ground reality of the protest revealed a different story, where Leftist organisations like the AISA were seen raising slogans of ‘Azadi-Azadi’ and ‘Jai Bheem’.

While AISA has not officially declared its support for the CJP, the All India President of AISA, Neha Bora, was at the forefront of the CJP protest. It is no secret that Left-wing students organistions like the AISA push their ideological and political agenda in the guise of raising students’ issues. And that’s exactly what Bora was seen doing in the pretext of demanding reforms in the education system.

Speaking to the media, Bora linked the issues of reforms in the education system and students’ rights with the UAPA accused Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. Blatantly whitewashing the charges against Khalid and Imam, Neha Bora claimed that ‘Godi Media’ and the ‘BJP IT Cell’ have declared them as traitors.

She referred to the anti-Hindu Delhi riots conspiracy accused as “ordinary students” and claimed that they were being subjected to “political prosecution”. She raised questions on the judiciary by pointing out that Khalid and Imam have been languishing in jail for years, as they were not granted bail. However, she cleverly conceals the fact that the Supreme Court had denied bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, observing that a prima facie case was made out against them in connection with the 2020 anti-Hindu Delhi riots conspiracy.

Neha Bora’s so-called students’ rights activism is not limited to whitewashing serious crimes like inciting riots or communal tensions; she openly advocates and promotes hatred against the Brahmin community in the name of countering caste inequality. In a post pinned on her X profile, Bora uses ‘Brahmanvaad’ (Brahmanism) as an umbrella term to refer to all kinds of discrimination prevalent in society. She defines Brahmanism as “the historical suppression of one section by another section of society”. By her logic, any discrimination in Indian society, even if it has nothing to do with caste, could be attributed to Brahmanism.

Students participating in the ongoing CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi staged a demonstration wearing masks of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Led by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, the protest has continued since June, with participants demanding accountability over examination irregularities, including the NEET UG paper leak controversy, and raising concerns over youth unemployment. Protesters have also called for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

As part of the demonstrations, participants have also banged steel plates with spoons, staged a symbolic funeral of the education system, and released open letters urging the Prime Minister to respond to their concerns. The protest continues with demands for greater transparency and reforms in the examination system.

- **Call for "strictest action"**: Opinion. Authorities monitor such protests; no widespread reports of illegality here.

The post mixes verified timing with partisan dismissal of a real youth-led exam protest. CJP is satirical in name but focused on education grievances.

Does the CJP only want Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation?

My answer would be no.

The Cockroach Janata Party isn't protesting because they want Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

Rather, they're doing so to incite people against PM Modi and the BJP under the guise of the NEET exam. They're creating an environment that sets a narrative, especially among young people, that Abhijeet Dipke and the CJP are truly fighting for us. That's why they initially launched a campaign stating that they don't support any political parties.

But when they started protesting everywhere, and people ignored them, they realized that leading people against the BJP isn't an easy task. Abhijeet Dipke then enlisted the help of Sonam Wangchuk and led her on a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar, Delhi. Still, there's no hope of success.

 Now they realized that CJP alone couldn't carry forward this protest, so gradually they began gathering all political parties and organizations. As you can see.

So will Dharmendra Pradhan resign now?

Will Modi and the BJP's popularity among the country's Gen Z diminish now?

The answer is: Absolutely not!

Because the way CJP is running this movement, and the people @abhijeet_dipke invites and gives them a platform, have nothing to do with this movement. Instead, they simply present their own agenda.

This allows the people of the country to understand what CJP's intentions are?
What does CJP want?
Why was CJP formed?
Who is behind CJP?

The questions are answered, and the cockroach Janta Party's protest fails.

This is why, from June 20th until today, July 14th, CJP has received disappointment instead of support from the people of the country.

Article:- Sonam Wangchuk’s Hunger Strike Enters 17th Day Amid:- 
Growing Health Concerns
Educator and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has reached the 17th day of an indefinite hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, sparking urgent appeals from political leaders and public figures for him to end his fast as his health rapidly deteriorates.
The Cause and Demands
Wangchuk joined an ongoing protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on June 28, 2026. The primary focus of the agitation is the demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged widespread irregularities in NEET and other national examinations.
Additionally, the protesters are seeking ₹1 crore in compensation for the families of students who allegedly died by suicide due to the fallout and stress of these examination irregularities.
Deteriorating Health
The prolonged fast is taking a severe toll on the 59-year-old activist. According to health updates shared by the CJP, Wangchuk has lost approximately 8.5 kilograms since beginning his strike. His blood glucose levels recently dropped to a concerning 67 mg/dL, and his blood pressure was recorded at 107/70 mm Hg. CJP spokespersons have stated that he is losing muscle mass and is in immense pain, warning that the coming days will be critical.
Growing Political and Public Support
As the medical crisis deepens, a growing chorus of prominent voices has expressed solidarity with the movement while urging Wangchuk to break his fast.
 *Political Leaders: Figures such as Akhilesh Yadav, Arvind Kejriwal, Uddhav Thackeray, and Mahua Moitra have voiced their support. Yadav and Kejriwal have publicly appealed to Wangchuk to end the fast, emphasizing that his life is too valuable to risk.
 *Civil Society: A group of eminent citizens, including writer Arundhati Roy and actors Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah, have also backed the demand for the Education Minister's resignation while urging the protesters to prioritize their health.
Despite the mounting pleas, Wangchuk has refused to end his strike, reportedly telling supporters to ask the government why they refuse to open a dialogue instead of asking him to eat. The protesters are now planning a peaceful march to Parliament on July 20, strategically timed to coincide with the opening day of the Monsoon Session, to further escalate their demands.

I support Sonam Wangchuk Sir ❤️

#SonamWangchuk #cjp_पार्टी
#HangerStrike

Actor Omi Vaidya, best known for playing Chatur in the film 3 Idiots, has expressed support for educator and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who entered the 17th day of his indefinite hunger strike.

In a video shared on social media, Vaidya referred to Aamir Khan's character Phunsukh Wangdu, widely regarded as being inspired by Wangchuk, and appealed to the public to pay attention to the activist's deteriorating health and the issues behind his protest.

"I don't want Phunsukh Wangdu to die," Vaidya said, urging people to learn more about Wangchuk's work and the reasons for his hunger strike. He also recalled meeting Wangchuk and described him as a remarkable individual.

According to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which is leading the protest at Jantar Mantar, Wangchuk has lost nearly 9 kilograms since beginning his fast, and his health has continued to decline.

The CJP's protest, which began over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, has expanded to include demands for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who allegedly died by suicide, and broader reforms in the examination system. The organisation has also announced a peaceful march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session.

body:
The lukewarm response that the Cockroach Janta Party founders are witnessing at Jantar Mantar are the signs of the times we live in. Maasive following on Insta and Fb does not translate into on ground support. The generation which follows you on social media, especially the one's born post 2000, will not be willing to hit the streets. Heck, they are not even willing to walk down the road to get their daily household needs, because Blinkit, Zomato, Swiggy and their fourth friend Amazon, are all there, at their service. 

If only Urban Company and Pronto had an option, where one could hire protestors on one's behalf to protest for a cause, then the dwindling prospects of Cockroach Janta Party would have got a massive boost, but as of now, that functionality is not provided, but you never know.

Second, the faces of this movement lack charisma and public connect. Abhijeet Dipke is no mass leader, like Arvind Kejriwal, his persona and his background does not make the person behind the screen go like 'Woah, he is the guy I am willing to take 1 day off from my office'. 

Saurav Das and the other fellow, who keeps dancing to songs of 1990's Bollywood are not even Twitter celebrities. Also why would the generation following them, born post 2000, vibe to songs of Bollywood movies of 90's and the era of 2000 to 2010.

I did enjoy their dance performance, but then I am not your target audience. Similarly for all of Sonam Wangchuk's achievements, he too is no Anna Hazare and India of 2026, is not India of 2012. Life in India has become more comfortable, while the income disparity remains, both these truths run parallel. 

The issue of NEET, Ethanol are the one's which the ruling government should be rightly questioned about and one can even see supporters of the current government taking them to task on these 2 major issues.

However, the fast unto death emotional blackmail type of protest is passe. It no longer appeals to the current generation, neither to the one's previous to them, who actually grew up watching such protests overturn governments of the day.

A few days back, came across a clip of my friend @Iyervval where he spoke about how we don't realize that how far India has come from the days of abject poverty and this is where the answer to the lack of response to CJP's Dharna Party lies.

More than anything else, it is the lack of imagination on behalf of CJP, and taking a traditional route, which finds itself a lost child in today's comfort at the drop of an app button playstore.

Meanwhile, it is activist and News influencer @tehseenp 's campaign highlighting the issue of Ethanol that is drawing more attention, where in the elected representatives of the day,are being grudingly forced to acknowledge the issue.

May be, just may be, CJP folks study what AIM and Tehseen are saying and take a leaf out of their book.

2026 is not 2012!

If only Urban Company and Pronto had an option, where one could hire protestors on one's behalf to protest for a cause, then the dwindling prospects of Cockroach Janta Party would have got a massive boost, but as of now, that functionality is not provided, but you never know. Second, the faces of this movement lack charisma and public connect. Abhijeet Dipke is no mass leader, like Arvind Kejriwal, his persona and his background does not make the person behind the screen go like 'Woah, he is the guy I am willing to take 1 day off from my office'. Saurav Das and the other fellow, who keeps dancing to songs of 1990's Bollywood are not even Twitter celebrities. Also why would the generation following them, born post 2000, vibe to songs of Bollywood movies of 90's and the era of 2000 to 2010. I did enjoy their dance performance, but then I am not your target audience. Similarly for all of Sonam Wangchuk's achievements, he too is no Anna Hazare and India of 2026, is not India of 2012. Life in India has become more comfortable, while the income disparity remains, both these truths run parallel. The issue of NEET, Ethanol are the one's which the ruling government should be rightly questioned about and one can even see supporters of the current government taking them to task on these 2 major issues. However, the fast unto death emotional blackmail type of protest is passe. It no longer appeals to the current generation, neither to the one's previous to them, who actually grew up watching such protests overturn governments of the day. A few days back, came across a clip of my friend @Iyervval where he spoke about how we don't realize that how far India has come from the days of abject poverty and this is where the answer to the lack of response to CJP's Dharna Party lies. More than anything else, it is the lack of imagination on behalf of CJP, and taking a traditional route, which finds itself a lost child in today's comfort at the drop of an app button playstore. Meanwhile, it is activist and News influencer @tehseenp 's campaign highlighting the issue of Ethanol that is drawing more attention, where in the elected representatives of the day,are being grudingly forced to acknowledge the issue. May be, just may be, CJP folks study what AIM and Tehseen are saying and take a leaf out of their book. 2026 is not 2012!

The #BJP led Union Government has repeatedly come under criticism over the handling of national-level entrance examinations, including #NEET. Despite multiple controversies, Union Education Minister #DharmendraPradhan continues to remain in office. What message does this send to the millions of students and parents across India who expect accountability from the government?

This year's NEET examination has been marred by numerous irregularities. Allegations have ranged from question paper leaks to students being allotted examination centres in foreign countries, while others, including candidates from Jammu & Kashmir, were assigned centres in distant states such as Rajasthan. These incidents have raised serious concerns about the transparency and fairness of the examination process. Yet, there appears to be little visible urgency or accountability from the Union Education Minister.

The responsibility for addressing these concerns ultimately rests with the Union Government. If such large scale irregularities have occurred, the Education Minister should take responsibility. Instead, there is a growing perception that the government has failed to adequately address the anxieties of students and parents.

Prime Minister #NarendraModi, who has the authority to act against his ministers, is perceived by critics as prioritising official foreign visits while dissatisfaction continues to grow at home. They argue that India's global image carries greater meaning when the concerns of its own citizens are addressed first.

Meanwhile, members of the Cockroach Janta Party (@CJP_2029) and education activist Sonam Wangchuk have been on a hunger strike for over two weeks, demanding accountability and reforms. Supporters of the protest believe the government's response has been inadequate despite the prolonged demonstration.

A government's greatest achievement is not merely governing the country, but governing in accordance with the aspirations and concerns of its people. When public sentiment and governmental priorities appear to diverge, celebrating achievements alone is unlikely to inspire confidence. Leadership earns respect through accountability, responsiveness, and a willingness to correct mistakes.

In Tamilnadu, the NEET examination has been associated with several student suicides over the years, making the issue especially sensitive. There is an urgent need either to abolish NEET altogether or to comprehensively reform the examination system so that it is conducted fairly, transparently, and without placing excessive psychological pressure on students. Every deserving student should be able to write the examination in a just, stress free, and equitable environment.

Above all, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan should accept responsibility for the latest irregularities and resign from his post. The demands raised through the CJP led protest deserve serious consideration, and those supporting the movement hope it succeeds in bringing meaningful accountability and reforms to India's education system. @abhijeet_dipke @CJP_for_India #PradhanGoBack

body:
Some people who joined CJP protest:

1) Arundhati Roy, who believes that Kashmir is not a part of India.

2) Colin Gonsalves, who filed a mercy petition for 26/11 terrorist Ajmal Kasab.

3) Prashant Bhushan, who approached Supreme Court at midnight to stop the hanging of terrorist Yakub Memon.

4) Nandita Narain, who sang "Bas naam rahega Allah ka" from CJP stage, a poem by Pakistani poet Faiz Ahmad Faiz.

5) Kunal Kamra, who said from CJP stage - "Yeh log Sita ke Pati ka naam lekar, Nita ke Pati ka kaam kar rahe hain" (They chant the name of Sita's husband, but they serve Nita's husband).

At what point does this even look like a protest against the NEET paper leak? If the objective was truly to seek justice for NEET students, the stage should have been given to the students who were affected by the paper leak, or to the parents whose children lost their lives due to the paper leak. Instead, the platform was given to the Islamo-left ecosystem. It clearly shows the CJP protest organizers' priorities and the real agenda behind the protest.

Sonam Wangchuk should also take a closer look at what is happening around him. He has been reduced to a pawn while others are using his credibility and public image to lend legitimacy to the movement.

A few days ago, Sonam Wangchuk himself remarked from the CJP stage that others were eating at the protest while he was on a hunger strike. He openly expressed disappointment and said - "If you cannot join me in an indefinite hunger strike, at least observe a one-day hunger strike, or skip one meal in solidarity." How many CJP protest organizers acted on his appeal?

He should analyze whether his struggle is being used to advance a broader political or ideological agenda rather than the cause that people believe he is representing, because the CJP protest appears to have become a platform for everything except the NEET paper leak.

By @AskAnshul

He was recently imprisoned by the Modi government on trumped up charges. He's currently on a hunger strike against educational irregularities that affect lakhs of children and their parents.

Many of them have voted once or twice in general elections. Some of them will vote for the first time in 2029. 

@RahulGandhi needs these voters on his side. Why wouldn't you use a platform of 23 million followers to woo them? 

Yes, the NSUI has creditably protested against the paper leaks.

It didn't make as much noise because the mainstream media ignored their protests. 

But what stops the Congress party leaders from using the CJP's platform and spreading the message of their protets to the wider public? 

This is or was your chance to bypass the mainstream media and reach out to voters with a bit of a clean slate. 

It requires a bizarre kind of insecurity to compete with an agitation rather than using it as an opportunity. 

Leave aside the political strategy for a minute. 

An activist known for educational innovation is on a hunger strike against the government. 

His health is deteriorating rapidly. The visuals of him weakening by the day are going through to millions of people on social media.

And Rahul Gandhi hasn't given a damn about it. How does that look on your CV?

Insensitive or callous?

ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಫ್ರೀಡಂ ಪಾರ್ಕ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಇಂದು CJP ವತಿಯಿಂದ ಬೃಹತ್ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ನಡೆಯಿತು. NEET ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಪತ್ರಿಕೆ ಸೋರಿಕೆ ಪ್ರಕರಣದ ಹೊಣೆ ಹೊತ್ತು ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಸಚಿವ ಧರ್ಮೇಂದ್ರ ಪ್ರಾಧಾನ್ ರಾಜೀನಾಮೆ ನೀಡಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನಾಕಾರರು ಆಗ್ರಹಿಸಿದರು.

ಇದೇ ವೇಳೆ, ಉಪವಾಸ ಸತ್ಯಾಗ್ರಹ ನಡೆಸುತ್ತಿರುವ ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ಹೋರಾಟಗಾರ ಸೋನಂ ವಾಂಗ್ಚುಕ್ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಐಕ್ಯತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬೆಂಬಲ ಸೂಚಿಸಿ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ ನಡೆಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು, ಯುವಕರು, ವಿವಿಧ ಸಂಘಟನೆಗಳ ಮುಖಂಡರು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರು ಭಾಗವಹಿಸಿ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾರದರ್ಶಕತೆ ಮತ್ತು ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ ಕ್ರಮ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳುವಂತೆ ಸರ್ಕಾರವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಾಯಿಸಿದರು.

ಆಯೋಜಕರ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ, ಸುಮಾರು 20 ಸಾವಿರಕ್ಕೂ ಅಧಿಕ ಜನರು ಈ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಗವಹಿಸಿದ್ದರು.

Sonam Wangchuk and Dharmendra Pradhan met over the National Education Policy in 2023.

If Dharmendra Pradhan could meet him and have a constructive discussion then, why shouldn't he meet him now? Dialogue is always better than deadlock. It is time for the Education Minister to meet Sonam Wangchuk over the concerns.

It is good that the Delhi Police acted on the Delhi High Court's orders, saved Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, and admitted him to the hospital. Why were none of the organizers present at the protest site at that time?

The organizers behind the CJP protest seem so driven by political ambitions that, if they believe Sonam Wangchuk's death could trigger a revolution or advance their political careers, they would prefer him to die. They are shameless and can stoop to any level.

The CJP protest is a platform for everything except the NEET paper leak. The stage was never given to the students who were affected by the paper leak, nor was it ever given to the parents whose children lost their lives because of the paper leak. Instead, the platform was given to the Islamo-left ecosystem:

1) Arundhati Roy, who believes that Kashmir is not a part of India.

2) Colin Gonsalves, who filed a mercy petition for 26/11 terrorist Ajmal Kasab.

तिलचट्टा जनता पार्टी के अभिजीत दीपके चलना तो अपने गुरु @ArvindKejriwal और @msisodia  की राह पर चाहते थे, लेकिन एक के बाद एक गलतियां करते रहे। उन्होंने अपने इस आंदोलन को छात्रों के हितों के लिए और गैर-राजनीतिक बताया, लेकिन पहली ही मांग @dpradhanbjp के इस्तीफे की रख दी। अरविंद केजरीवाल ने अनशन के लिए अन्ना को चुना था, तो @abhijeet_dipke ने @Wangchuk66 को। पहले छात्रों के लिए गैर-राजनीतिक आंदोलन की बात करते रहे, लेकिन ऐसा लगा कि मजमा नहीं जम रहा है, तो कांग्रेस समेत तमाम राजनीतिक पार्टियों के नेताओं को आने के लिए पत्र भी लिख दिया।

रही बात नीट एग्जाम की, तो वो सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न कराया जा चुका है। ऐसे में अभिजीत दीपके और उनकी टीम के सामने सोनम वांगचुक का आमरण अनशन सम्मानजनक ढंग से तुड़वाने का जुगाड़ करना ही एकमात्र विकल्प है।

Some people who joined CJP protest:

1) Arundhati Roy, who believes that Kashmir is not a part of India.

2) Colin Gonsalves, who filed a mercy petition for 26/11 terrorist Ajmal Kasab.

3) Prashant Bhushan, who approached Supreme Court at midnight to stop the hanging of terrorist Yakub Memon.

4) Nandita Narain, who sang "Bas naam rahega Allah ka" from CJP stage, a poem by Pakistani poet Faiz Ahmad Faiz.

5) Kunal Kamra, who said from CJP stage - "Yeh log Sita ke Pati ka naam lekar, Nita ke Pati ka kaam kar rahe hain" (They chant the name of Sita's husband, but they serve Nita's husband).

At what point does this even look like a protest against the NEET paper leak? If the objective was truly to seek justice for NEET students, the stage should have been given to the students who were affected by the paper leak, or to the parents whose children lost their lives due to the paper leak. Instead, the platform was given to the Islamo-left ecosystem. It clearly shows the CJP protest organizers' priorities and the real agenda behind the protest.

Sonam Wangchuk should also take a closer look at what is happening around him. He has been reduced to a pawn while others are using his credibility and public image to lend legitimacy to the movement.

A few days ago, Sonam Wangchuk himself remarked from the CJP stage that others were eating at the protest while he was on a hunger strike. He openly expressed disappointment and said - "If you cannot join me in an indefinite hunger strike, at least observe a one-day hunger strike, or skip one meal in solidarity." How many CJP protest organizers acted on his appeal?

He should analyze whether his struggle is being used to advance a broader political or ideological agenda rather than the cause that people believe he is representing, because the CJP protest appears to have become a platform for everything except the NEET paper leak.

The Hijacking of Student Anger: Exposing Abhijeet Dipke, CJP, and the Political Drift of the NEET Protests

The NEET paper leak crisis of 2026 triggered one of the biggest student movements in recent years. Lakhs of aspirants saw their futures thrown into uncertainty, while several families suffered unimaginable loss. The protests initially focused on a single demand—accountability for the examination system and action against those responsible for the leak. However, critics argue that what began as a student-led movement gradually transformed into a broader political platform under the leadership of Abhijeet Dipke and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

Dipke, a former Aam Aadmi Party social media operative, launched CJP in May 2026. The organisation rapidly gained millions of followers online and positioned itself as the voice of frustrated students. Its stated demands included the resignation of the Education Minister, compensation for affected families, and structural reforms to prevent future paper leaks. Yet as protests expanded across cities, observers noted that the movement increasingly attracted political organisations and ideological groups whose agendas extended well beyond education.

Left-leaning student organisations such as the Students' Federation of India (SFI), the All India Students' Association (AISA), and Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) became prominent participants. Opposition leaders and public figures also visited protest sites, while activist Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike added national attention. Critics argued that these developments shifted the focus from examination reforms to wider political narratives.

The controversy intensified after actor Prakash Raj publicly stated at a protest that he would not chant Jai Shri Ram. His remarks, along with comments about not caring if protesters were labelled terrorists or Pakistanis, became one of the most debated moments of the movement. Separately, a performance of Faiz Ahmed Faiz's poetry at the protest drew complaints from Hindu organisations, which alleged that it hurt religious sentiments. These incidents fuelled accusations that the protests were no longer centred solely on student welfare.

Dipke himself attracted criticism after stating during an interview that if he were Muslim like Umar Khalid, he would already be in jail. Around the same period, photographs showing CJP spokesperson Saurav Das with Umar Khalid circulated online, leading critics to question the ideological associations surrounding the movement. Although supporters dismissed these concerns as political attacks, opponents argued that they reflected a broader shift away from educational issues.

Questions were also raised about funding and organisational transparency. CJP maintained that its activities were driven by volunteers and public support. However, critics questioned how a movement that organised nationwide protests, legal campaigns, and extensive media outreach could sustain such operations without greater financial backing or institutional support.

Ultimately, the biggest criticism of CJP is not that it protested the NEET paper leak, but that it allegedly allowed the movement to become politically and ideologically polarised. Many believe students deserved a united campaign focused exclusively on examination reforms and accountability. Instead, the protests became associated with controversies involving religion, political symbolism, and ideological conflict.

Whether one views CJP as a genuine youth movement or a politically influenced campaign, the debate surrounding its role continues. The 2026 NEET protests remain a reminder of how quickly a movement built around legitimate student grievances can evolve into a much broader political confrontation.

यह बेहद खतरनाक प्रवृत्ति बनती जा रही है। आज मीडिया कर्मियों के साथ दुर्व्यवहार हो रहा है, कल स्थिति मारपीट तक भी पहुंच सकती है।

विडंबना यह है कि एक तरफ कहा जाता है कि मीडिया CJP protest कवरेज नहीं करती, और जब मीडिया कवरेज के लिए पहुंचती है तो उसे "गोदी मीडिया" कहकर हंगामा किया जाता है। ऐसे माहौल में पत्रकारों की सुरक्षा गंभीर चिंता का विषय है।

जब तक उनकी सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित न हो, मीडिया संस्थानों को भी ऐसे आयोजनों की कवरेज के दौरान अपने पत्रकारों की सुरक्षा को प्राथमिकता देनी चाहिए। किसी भी खबर से बढ़कर एक पत्रकार की जान और सुरक्षा है।

This is becoming an extremely dangerous trend. Today, media personnel face mistreatment; tomorrow, the situation could escalate to physical assault.

The irony is that, on one hand, there are complaints that the media fails to provide coverage of CJP protest, yet when the media arrives to cover an event, an uproar is raised by labeling them "Godi Media" (lapdog media). In such an atmosphere, the safety of journalists is a matter of serious concern.

Until their safety is guaranteed, media organizations must prioritize the security of their journalists while covering such events. A journalist's life and safety are far more important than any news story.

#Bengaluru: Supporters of climate activist Sonam Wangchuk gathered at Freedom Park on Sunday in solidarity after he was removed from his hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and shifted to Safdarjung Hospital following 21 days of fasting over alleged examination paper leaks. 

The protest, organised by the  Cockroach Janata  Party (CJP), drew students, activists and civil society members, who demanded accountability and justice for students.

The Bengaluru gathering was attended by more than 1000 people, builds on CJP's ongoing campaign in the city, which has urged citizens to sustain public participation and  the government over issues affecting students and education particularly the NEET paper leaks.

  Wangchuk has appealed to supporters to join the 'Chalo Sansad' march in Delhi on Monday.

body:
A friend wrote the other day that LinkedIn posts are like moral science stories. Mine here is sounding like that i think. Just watched SBS World News in Australia, covering environmentalist and engineer Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike and his removal from Jantar Mantar by police over concerns for his health. Hence the outpouring. 

Like many in the diaspora, I follow the news from back home closely, but what troubles me these days is not just the news itself, but how difficult it has become to talk about India without being immediately pushed into one political camp or another. You know, question anything about the current Modi govt and be branded anti-national or a Pakistani.

Been following Jantar Mantar. To be honest, I'm not a fan of Abhijeet Dipke's voice. Sorry that is just my aesthetics at play, very shallow yes :), but whatever one's politics, the Cockroach Janata Party is focussing on something that is affecting the futures of millions of young people and deserve to be discussed seriously, not dismissed because they are politically inconvenient.

I know perfectly well how things function in India. I remember applying for my first passport in 1993. The police verification officer found everything in order, but still hinted that he expected chai-pani ka kharcha. Also, my father, a government servant, always told me that the person who gives a bribe is no better than the person who takes one. Ofc, I was going to stick to this, especially when I was a student and verging on broke. Thankfully, I still received my passport.

Corruption, bureaucratic hurdles and the struggle for opportunities are not new problems in India. Everyone knows that, come on! But then I scroll through my feed and see some friends calling these protesters "planted" to smear the government. Really? Are they not seeing what's right in front of us? The job crisis, the falling rupee, the shaky economic indicators – it's all there. Ugggghhhhhh.

How is it wrong to agree with facts that are clearly visible? I love India - no one can take that away from me but this whole "all is well, Modi is God" narrative? That, I genuinely don't get. 

Btw, do watch News Pinch @TheNewspinch. They have some of the most powerful interviews from this protest at Jantar Mantar.

Ladakh ka 'Hero' ya Drama King? Sachchai aap decide karo!

1/ Sonam Wangchuk Jantar Mantar pe indefinite hunger strike kar rahe hain. "Main mar jaunga lekin peeche nahi hatunga!" Bollywood dialogue jaisa. Lekin kya yeh asliyat hai ya political drama? Facts se samjhte hain. #SonamWangchuk

2/ Ladakh Mudda: Sixth Schedule, Statehood, border security ke naam pe protest. Centre se baat nahi bani toh fast?
Lekin yaad rakho – Ladakh strategic border area hai (China-Pak). 2019 ke baad UT bana, development ho raha hai (roads, tourism, infra). Multiple talks hue (Feb-May 2026). Har cheez ko "vaada khilafi" bolna selective hai. National security se upar kuch nahi!

3/ Exam Scam (NEET/CJP): Wangchuk join karke viral hue. Students ke liye sympathy. Health kharab, hospital shift.
Lekin scams har system mein hote hain. Government investigate kar rahi. Minister resignation + ₹1 Cr compensation – yeh reform hai ya politics? Real solution coaching mafia, paper leaks pe action hai, na ki drama fast!

4/ Selective activism ka issue: Climate change pe awaaz acchi, lekin China encroachment, internal Ladakh problems, demographic change pe balanced view kyun nahi? "I may die" bolke sympathy harvest karna easy hai. Asli kaam chupke se hota hai – soldiers, engineers, teachers ka.

5/ Hunger strike Gandhi ji ke time tha British ke against. Aaj democratic desh mein har issue pe yeh karna attention seeking lagta hai. Dialogue, RTI, court – yeh hai asli rasta. Ladakh ke log bhi divided hain – kuch development chahte hain.

6/ Conclusion: Wangchuk ji, passion accha hai lekin drama band kijiye. Facts, constructive talk aur development pe focus kijiye. India tarakki kar raha hai – border strong, education sudhar raha. Selective outrage se desh nahi banega!
Bharat Mata ki Jai! 🇮🇳
Share karo agar sahi lage → #SonamWangchuk #Ladakh #NEETScam #ExamReform #BharatFirst #JantarMantar #IndiaRising

'Say Yes or No, But Talk': Anna Hazare Appeals to Centre Over Sonam Wangchuk's Hunger Strike
https://t.co/yPWCt814pE
Social activist Anna Hazare strongly urged the Union government to immediately initiate dialogue with educationist Sonam Wangchuk. 

Anna stated that the government should not "test his limits" or patience, emphasizing that there is no harm in holding discussions even if the administration ultimately chooses to say yes or no to the demands.

Anna's public support came on the 21st day of Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. Wangchuk is demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak scandal.

Anna explicitly questioned the government's stance, asking, "Say yes or no to his demands, but what is wrong in holding discussions?". 

He warned authorities not to wait for a "tragic outcome" regarding Wangchuk's rapidly deteriorating health. 

Commenting on the situation, Anna noted that the matter concerns society and must be handled peacefully, adding that forceful actions or pulling and dragging by police only make the issue more complicated. 

Anna's appeal followed an incident where the Delhi Police forcibly removed Wangchuk from his protest site and shifted him to Safdarjung Hospital due to worsening health indicators, including severe dehydration and dropping potassium levels.

An insightful and balanced piece that captures both the human story and the public policy dimensions of Sonam Wangchuk's protest with remarkable clarity.

Key Facts (UPSC & Current Affairs)

Sonam Wangchuk has completed a 21-day Hunger Strike, becoming the face of the CJP (Cockroach Janta Party) protest at Jantar Mantar.

The protest demands the Resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged lapses in NEET and CBSE examinations.

Authorities removed Wangchuk from the protest site and shifted him to an ambulance amid concerns over his deteriorating Health.

Wangchuk has repeatedly stated that the movement is Non-Political, focusing on Accountability, Educational Reforms, and Transparency.

A Parliament March was planned to press for the Education Minister's resignation.

Wangchuk is a Ramon Magsaysay Award (2018) recipient, honoured for Community-Driven Education, Innovation, and Rural Development in Ladakh.

He earlier led movements for Ladakh's Climate Protection, Autonomy, and Constitutional Safeguards after the Abrogation of Article 370.

He is widely known as the inspiration behind Phunsukh Wangdu in the film 3 Idiots, though he has maintained distance from that association.

Despite criticism and skepticism, Public Support at Jantar Mantar continued to grow throughout the protest.

🚨 BREAKING | Jantar Mantar Protest Update

▶️ Delhi Police forcefully shifted environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk to Safdarjung Hospital on the 21st day of his indefinite hunger strike.

▶️ Police said the action was taken following medical advice and directions of the Delhi High Court.

▶️ According to the hospital's medical bulletin, Wangchuk showed signs of dehydration and metabolic abnormalities but refused IV fluids, medication, and oral rehydration.

▶️ Protesters alleged that police personnel, including officers in plain clothes, entered the protest site, surrounded the stage, and forcibly removed Wangchuk.

▶️ Demonstrators claimed they formed a human chain to stop the operation, but police used force and allegedly assaulted several protesters.

▶️ CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke launched another indefinite hunger strike, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak and calling for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to resign.

▶️ During Dipke's address, a woman allegedly threw an ink-like liquid at him before being detained by police.

▶️ Sonam Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo urged that no medicine or IV treatment be administered without the consent of the family and his treating doctors.

▶️ Large numbers of protesters reassembled at Jantar Mantar later in the day, vowing to continue the movement and the planned Parliament March.

⚠️ The allegations made by protesters and political leaders are their claims. Delhi Police maintains that its action was carried out in accordance with medical advice and the High Court's directions.

so basically: 22 lakh families affected

#SonamWangchuk Hospitalised After 21-Day #HungerStrike; #CJP Founder #AbhishekDipke attacked with #Ink | Protest Sparks Political Row

Activist, engineer, and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk was shifted to #Safdarjung Hospital by #DelhiPolice on Saturday after his indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar entered its 21st day and his health reportedly deteriorated.

According to Delhi Police, the action was taken on the advice of medical experts and in compliance with the directions of the Delhi High Court, which had ordered regular monitoring of Wangchuk's health. In an official statement, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, said Wangchuk was moved to the hospital for "essential medical care" and appealed to protesters to vacate the protest site peacefully.

Supporters of Wangchuk, however, alleged that plainclothes police personnel entered the protest stage, blocked public view using white sheets, and removed him against his will. They argued that the court had directed authorities to monitor his health rather than forcibly end the protest. These claims have not been independently verified.

The protest is linked to demands for accountability over the alleged #NEET examination #PaperLeak, with demonstrators seeking the resignation of Union #EducationMinister #DharmendraPradhan and broader reforms to the examination system.

Following Wangchuk's removal, #CockroachJanataParty founder #AbhijeetDipke announced an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. During the protest, a woman allegedly threw blue ink at Dipke, briefly creating chaos at the site. Reacting to the incident, he said, "Blue is my colour. Jai Bhim."

Before being taken to the hospital, Wangchuk addressed supporters, saying, "I've grown weak from the outside, but I'm strong from within." His supporters claim he lost around 9.5 kilograms during the fast.

The incident has triggered sharp political reactions, with opposition leaders criticising the police action, while Delhi Police maintain that the decision was taken solely to ensure Wangchuk received urgent medical treatment in view of his deteriorating health.

His supporters claim he lost around 9.5 kilograms during the fast. Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's father on Saturday criticised the Centre over its handling of the ongoing student protests, questioning how the government could be so "merciless" towards students and asking whether it was waiting for someone to die.

Bhagwan Dipke's remarks came hours after his son launched an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar following the hospitalisation of activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital after his health deteriorated during a 20-day fast over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination.

Speaking to a Marathi news channel from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Bhagwan Dipke expressed concern over his son's health while urging the government to engage with the protesting students.

"As a father, I am concerned about Abhijeet. I pray that God gives wisdom to Prime Minister Narendra Modi so that better sense prevails and the government listens to the agitating students. Students across the country are on hunger strike. Is the government waiting for someone to die?" he said.

He accused the government of ignoring the concerns of students and questioned its alleged indifference.

"Are these students from Pakistan or any other country? They are Indians. How can the government behave so mercilessly towards them?" he asked.

Bhagwan Dipke also warned that if the government continued to ignore the protesters' demands, he and other family members would travel to Delhi and join the indefinite hunger strike.

His wife also expressed concern over the situation, saying the government should have waited until after the planned July 20 Parliament march before shifting Wangchuk to the hospital.

"The protest in Delhi was peaceful. Abhijeet began his indefinite fast after Sonam Wangchuk was taken to hospital. We are worried about him. The government should have taken a decision after July 20," she said.

She added that only the government knew why the agitation was not being taken seriously.

It is good that the Delhi Police acted on the Delhi High Court's orders, saved Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, and admitted him to the hospital. Why were none of the organizers present at the protest site at that time?

The organizers behind the CJP protest seem so driven by political ambitions that, if they believe Sonam Wangchuk's death could trigger a revolution or advance their political careers, they would prefer him to die. They are shameless and can stoop to any level.

The CJP protest is a platform for everything except the NEET paper leak. The stage was never given to the students who were affected by the paper leak, nor was it ever given to the parents whose children lost their lives because of the paper leak. 
Instead, the platform was given to the Islamo-left ecosystem:
1) Arundhati Roy, who believes that Kashmir is not a part of India.
2) Colin Gonsalves, who filed a mercy petition for 26/11 terrorist Ajmal Kasab.
3) Prashant Bhushan, who approached the Supreme Court at midnight to stop the hanging of terrorist Yakub Memon.
4) Nandita Narain, who sang "Bas naam rahega Allah ka" from the CJP stage, a poem by Pakistani poet Faiz Ahmad Faiz.
5) Kunal Kamra, who said from the CJP stage - "Yeh log Sita ke Pati ka naam lekar, Nita ke Pati ka kaam kar rahe hain" (They chant the name of Sita's husband, but they serve Nita's husband.)
6) Prakash Raj, who said from the CJP stage - "They chant Jai Shri Ram, but I will chant Jai Samvidhan".

At what point does this even look like a protest against the NEET paper leak? Which of these statements is for NEET students?

Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan should have stepped down much earlier, not because of the CJP protest or Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike, but because of accountability. It is not just about the NEET paper leak, but also about one-sided UGC equity regulations and CBSE OSM flaws. 
These are his failures, and he should take responsibility for them.

And today, if such an atmosphere has been created where, on one stage, people who are terrorist sympathizers are present, people who are mocking Hinduism are present, people who are Naxal sympathizers are present, and people who have filed mercy petitions for terrorists and stood in court on their behalf are present, and they are spreading their agenda from the stage in the name of protest, then the CJP organizers are responsible for this. They are fully aware of what they are doing and of the statements being made from the stage.

They are so shameless that when the Delhi Police arrived to take Sonam Wangchuk to the hospital, not a single CJP organizer was present at the protest site because they were elsewhere, staying in their comfort zone.

They are using Sonam Wangchuk. And if they believe that his death during the hunger strike could benefit their political careers and serve their agenda, they will leave him to die.

Sonam Wangchuk joined the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar.

He began an indefinite hunger strike on June 28, 2026, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET-UG paper leaks and exam irregularities.

The Delhi High Court ordered daily medical monitoring and directed authorities to provide necessary medical intervention to protect his life.

On July 18 (Day 21 of the fast), Delhi Police shifted Wangchuk to Safdarjung Hospital, citing the court's order, expert medical advice, significant weight loss, and low blood sugar.

Delhi Police said protesters caused slight commotion during the transfer, but officers exercised maximum restraint.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged Wangchuk was forcibly detained and accused police of assaulting protesters during the transfer.

Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali J. Angmo, alleged she was not allowed to carry her mobile phone into his eighth-floor room, with access beyond the sixth floor heavily restricted by police.

Angmo also claimed medical reports were withheld and personal lawyers and doctors were not allowed to meet Wangchuk.

She publicly opposed any oral or intravenous treatment without the consent of the family and Wangchuk's monitoring doctors, questioned the need for hospitalization, said he had appeared fine the previous day, and noted no official police or hospital response to these specific allegations had been reported.

#SonamWangchuk

Abolishing or “regularising” NEET is not the central demand of the main CJP-led student protests in Delhi. Their focus is accountability for the leak, the minister’s resignation, and systemic exam reforms.

Whereas TN has been asking to scrap NEET completely . For the youth  in North who are actively protesting , Minister’s resignation will be a big win but for TN Students and political parties, scrapping NEET will be the major win.

I only hope those who are voicing out here in TN understands the basic difference. While I agree that we should stand in solidarity with the students, your idea of NEET and theirs is completely different!! If they also voice out to scrap the exam, TN protests will get intense. Otherwise, it will be a customary protest and youths here in TN will move on.  

I’m completely against NEET . Corrupted system can’t conduct a clean entrance examination, there will always be room for malpractice.  If the Government feels that the marks scored by students of State Board or CBSE aren’t enough, you are saying that the curriculum is inferior. So, change the curriculum to superior format, so students can study and get their medical seats without any entrance exams 👍

Ardent BJP supporters too are no fans of India's Education Minister, Mr Dharmendra Pradhan. The opposition exists in a democracy to raise issues against the ruling government, so why would they leave the chance to ask for the resignation of Mr Pradhan. In all this, the online moment of Cockroach Janta Party, sensed an oppurtunity and they went all guns blazing. Again, completely regular and obvious thing to do in a democracy. They sensed the burning issue affecting the youth of India, and had also the support of the parents of these youngsters, which was the NEET leak scandal.

BJP top brass did not budge and stuck to backing it's blue eyed Education Minister. This only worked better for CJP and it's handlers, and they took the movement offline.

As the imprints of AAP and connections with it's top leaders became more clear, the public did not give it the support which Dipke thought they would.

However since the issue of Pradhan not being sacked has hit a raw nerve among the youth, there are various groups within the protestors who now have come together. What we saw today is the intersection of State-Ruling government-Peaceful protestors-Criminals-Negotiations-Opposition which in a nutshell my friend is called a Democracy.

Why didn't #Vijay i.e. CM of TN support the 
#JantarMantarprotest ?

#CMVijay had already written to the #PM seeking steps to ban #NEET as soon as he became Chief Minister. So, his stand against #NEET is already clear.

Now, coming to the #CJP protest, it has three demands:
1. Release #SonamWangchuk 
2. Provide ₹1 crore compensation to the affected students' families.
3. Resignation of the Education Minister.

I agree with the first two demands. But I am skeptical about the third.

A paper leak occurred, investigations were conducted, those responsible were identified, and action was taken. The system is also being moved towards Computer-Based Tests with stronger encryption reduce such incidents.

If the demand was to #BanNEET because the system itself is flawed, we should support that. But demanding only a minister's resignation doesn't solve the root problem.

If #CMVijay supports this, it would set a dangerous precedent. Tomorrow, every issue could simply become a demand for a minister's resignation. Which is not justified !!!

Ministers can change. Unless the system is corrected, the same issue can happen again under someone else. 

I'm not a blind supporter of #CJP. I have my own reservations.

So, when I myself have doubts, I understand why #CMVijay chose not to comment.

That said, the protest should never have turned violent. The ruling Central Government i.e. #BJP must take responsibility for that.

POV : I'm not a #BJP supporter. This is simply my personal opinion.

A Neet student says "this is my last day at the protest" 🚨

17 year old Rushi Mehra -
I am going back home. I can't do this anymore. There are literally 5 goons around every genuine student. My brother and sister were protecting a Delhi Police officer because we had met him before, gave toffees to him and he told us if any problem occurs we can reach out to him. Last night, he didn't even have a stick in his hand. He was just asking everyone to move aside.

Suddenly, 10-15 goons attacked him and shouted, "Tujhe bhi Ratan Lal banayenge." I didn't understand it at that moment but when we searched on google, we found that Ratan Lal was a police officer who lost his life during a riot in 2020.

We were shocked. The most shocking part is that even the people leading the protest know about this but they are not doing anything. I want a career and I don't want to get into any trouble. If you are a student, just get out of this facade. Otherwise, you could end up ruining your career along with these goons." 

I hope she reaches home safely after exposing the reality of CJP with so much courage

I fully endorse the views expressed by @annamalai_k. Protest is a democratic right, but timely dialogue and addressing people is the responsibility of a democratic government.

The question that deserves an answer is simple: Why does meaningful engagement so often come only after a crisis escalates?

As an Ex-Serviceman, I have witnessed this pattern repeatedly. Since 2015, veterans have peacefully protested at Jantar Mantar over issues such as OROP implementation and other long pending grievances. Farmers have protested. Students have protested. In each case, many participants raised genuine concerns that deserved timely engagement.

We should not dismiss every protester as "anti national" simply because some individuals and political parties may attempt to hijack a movement. The law must deal firmly with those who incite violence or attack police, journalists, or public property. But genuine grievances should never be ignored because of the actions of a few.

I am often attacked on social media for expressing these views. Let me be clear: I am a nationalist. My loyalty is to the Nation, not to any individual or political party.

Supporting the government when it is right and questioning it when it falls short are both acts of patriotism.

Despite repeated representations, this government has neither resolved the genuine grievances of ex servicemen nor fully complied with many judgments of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT), the High Courts, and the Supreme Court. 

Leadership is measured not only by decisive action, but also by the willingness to listen. Humility strengthens leadership; "high headedness" creates distance between a government and its people. India's youth, farmers, and veterans deserve to be heard before frustration turns into unrest.

Nation First. Truth First. Always. 🇮🇳

@PMOIndia @narendramodi @BJP4India @BJP4TamilNadu #NEET #CJP

Over the past many years, I have taken a personal stand in support of the NEET examination, arguing that it brought uniformity in student selection across the country and gave students from underprivileged backgrounds a real shot at pursuing their dream of medical education. In the last 5 years, the NEET UG question paper has leaked thrice. Imagine the amount of pressure that it puts on students, who had to go through the examination process yet another time when the system that was supposed to bring in uniformity was failing. Yet there was no accountability, and I believe strongly that it was that moment that brought in a shift in the minds of the students to take to the streets to cry their hearts out. 

Protest is a fundamental right in a Democracy. The pertinent question, however, is this: why did the BJP-led Central Government take so long to initiate a dialogue with the protestors? Why was meaningful engagement delayed until the protest had escalated to a flashpoint? What kept you waiting?

The students and the people who are leading them also have a responsibility here. It is natural that when a protest stays on for weeks, people with vested interests will take the stage to air views that are either completely irrelevant to the initial demands of the protests or would try to completely hijack it to serve their agenda. If you remain silent and let these people with vested interests further their agenda, then you are deviating from your core objectives. Please do not let it happen!

I urge the BJP-led Central Government to engage in meaningful dialogue, uphold transparency, and take swift, appropriate action to address the concerns at hand. The strength of any nation lies in the confidence its youth place in its institutions. If our students lose faith in the fairness and credibility of our education system, we are jeopardising the future of our nation.

body:
Let me give you a reality check.

India has seen protests before. But this one is different.

Earlier, many mass movements were led by people who already had stable jobs, financial security, and a safety net. They could afford to spend days on the streets because losing one week didn’t mean losing their future.

Today’s youth don’t have that privilege.

Many of the faces you saw at the CJP protest weren’t just NEET aspirants. Some were former aspirants. Some had spent 6, 8, even 10 years preparing for one competitive exam after another. Some crossed 30. Some exhausted their savings. Some watched friends move on while they remained trapped in an endless cycle of forms, postponements, paper leaks, vacancies that never came, and recruitment processes that stretched for years.

People mock them by asking, “Does a 30 year old look like a NEET aspirant?”

No. They look like the outcome of a broken system with nothing to lose. 

They look like someone who was told since childhood that education would change their life, only to discover that merit means little when exams are repeatedly cancelled, recruitment is delayed, and opportunities keep shrinking.

History shows the same pattern.

The JP Movement of the 1970s wasn’t just about politics. It was fuelled by students angry over unemployment, inflation, corruption, and a government that had stopped listening.

The Mandal Commission protests were about more than reservations, they reflected deep anxiety over limited government jobs and a generation terrified about its future.

Across the world, whether it was the Arab Spring or student-led movements in Europe and Latin America, prolonged unemployment and the feeling of having no future became powerful forces behind public unrest.

When an entire generation starts believing that hard work no longer guarantees dignity, the problem is no longer individual failure. It becomes a failure of governance.

A government cannot promise every citizen a government job.

But it is responsible for creating opportunities, conducting fair and timely recruitment, protecting the integrity of examinations, and ensuring that young people don’t spend the best years of their lives waiting for a result that never arrives.

Hope is not built through slogans.

Hope is built when effort is rewarded.

And when that hope disappears, frustration doesn’t stay inside coaching classrooms forever.

One day, it reaches the streets.

When thousands of young people decide that protesting feels more meaningful than studying for the next exam, that should alarm every government, regardless of which party is in power.

Because the biggest crisis isn’t unemployment.

It’s a generation slowly losing faith that tomorrow will be better than today 🙏🏻

By injecting politics into the protest and attempting to portray the students movement as one against the #TVKVijay‌ government, those who directed their hostility toward Chief Minister Vijay and the TVK administration have now been exposed by actress @ungalsanam.

At a time when the protest against the alleged #NEET question paper leak was meant to remain focused solely on that issue, some participants carried placards reading, 'We need JanaNayagam, not JanaNayagan,' thereby politicizing the students movement. Sanam Shetty has exposed what she describes as the agenda of DMK agents who sought to divert the protest for political purposes. While CJP members have been protesting in Delhi for over 20 days, many of those who had spent the same period discussing and celebrating the FIFA World Cup and new film releases suddenly chose to unleash their hostility when the subject became Vijay. Sanam Shetty has exposed the double standards of these individuals.

The students protest is gradually being diverted from its original purpose. Particularly in Tamilnadu, efforts are being made to steer it in a different direction. While the CJP protesters and the students are demanding only the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, some individuals, unable to come to terms with their political defeat, are using the movement as an outlet for their resentment. By calling this out openly, Sanam Shetty has exposed these elements, and she deserves appreciation for doing so.

body:
Nine years ago, S Anitha became the first victim of NEET in Tamil Nadu, and one of the most prominent faces of Tamil Nadu’s fight against NEET.

In 2017, the 17-year-old from Ariyalur had scored 1,176 out of 1,200 marks in her Class 12 Tamil Nadu State Board exams. Her medical cut-off score was 196.75 out of 200 — marks that would have placed her among medical aspirants under Tamil Nadu’s earlier admission system.

But that year, NEET became mandatory for medical admissions. Anitha, who had prepared through the state-board syllabus, could not secure a medical seat through the national entrance exam. She became one of the earliest voices opposing NEET in Tamil Nadu, arguing that a common entrance test would disadvantage students from rural areas, government schools and marginalised communities.

Anitha’s brother S. Manirathnam, who has now joined the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest in Delhi, says her fight was deeply personal.

He says Anitha was raised by their father, a daily wage labourer, after their mother died when she was seven. He recalls that Anitha wanted to become a doctor because their mother’s death due to an illness had shaped her dream of entering medicine.

“She wanted to become a doctor because she had seen the suffering caused by the lack of medical care,” Manirathnam said, recalling his sister’s journey.

Anitha joined the legal battle against NEET and became one of the petitioners before the Supreme Court, seeking relief for Tamil Nadu students. The Court did not grant the exemption sought by the state, and days later, on 1 September 2017, Anitha died by suicide at her home in Ariyalur.

Speaking about the impact of NEET on his family, Manirathnam said, “NEET has destroyed my family.”

Years later, he has joined the CJP protest, saying Tamil Nadu’s opposition to NEET began with students like Anitha, who questioned whether a single national entrance exam could account for the inequalities faced by students across the country.

Thanks: The Quint

VIDEO | Delhi: After meeting the injured in July 20th CJP protest over NEET issue, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) says, “Several students were injured in yesterday's protest. Several police personnel were also injured. Many of the injured students and police personnel were brought to RML Hospital. Today, I came here to meet all those who were injured. We have been informed that, except for one girl, everyone else has been discharged. All the injured students and all the injured police personnel have been discharged. One girl is in the ICU and is in critical condition…They may be in other hospitals as well. We do not have that data. What is circulating on social media is that there were 10 people, but we do not have any authentic figure…From here, we are going to Parliament Street Police Station because we have seen on social media that several students are missing and their parents fear that the police may have taken them away. There are also reports that false FIRs have been filed against several students…Today, we have also launched a helpline so that anyone who needs legal assistance or medical assistance can receive that help.”

He is Vibhu Gautam.

He made abusive remarks against the Indian Army during the CJP protest.

After his video went viral, some people decided that he should be handed over to the police. However, when they went to his house, they found out that his father is disabled. Seeing his father's situation, they decided not to pursue getting him arrested. Instead, they asked him to apologize, and he later recorded and posted a video apologizing.

Is it wrong to protest against the NEET paper leak or to demand the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan? No, not at all.

But that is not what he did. Instead, he came to the protest and started making abusive remarks against the Indian Army. He is not a child who cannot distinguish between right and wrong. He is old enough to understand the remarks he is making and the legal consequences of his actions.

His mindset led him to believe that it was the moment to turn India into another Nepal or Bangladesh. Many people like him also fail to understand that when they move away from the actual cause of a protest and engage in propaganda and anti-India activities, they may face serious legal consequences. Their careers and futures could be affected. In his case, even his father had to apologize because of his son's actions.

This period of unrest is temporary. The protests will eventually end. Those with political ambitions will move on and continue with politics. But common people like us may end up facing the consequences.

In the end, all that remains is regret.
By the time you realize the cost of your actions, the damage is already done. It can leave behind years of legal trouble, a damaged reputation, lost opportunities, and a burden that lasts far longer than the protest itself.

Nine years ago, S Anitha became the first victim of NEET in Tamil Nadu, and one of the most prominent faces of Tamil Nadu’s fight against NEET.

In 2017, the 17-year-old from Ariyalur had scored 1,176 out of 1,200 marks in her Class 12 Tamil Nadu State Board exams. Her medical cut-off score was 196.75 out of 200 — marks that would have placed her among medical aspirants under Tamil Nadu’s earlier admission system.

But that year, NEET became mandatory for medical admissions. Anitha, who had prepared through the state-board syllabus, could not secure a medical seat through the national entrance exam. She became one of the earliest voices opposing NEET in Tamil Nadu, arguing that a common entrance test would disadvantage students from rural areas, government schools and marginalised communities.

Anitha’s brother S. Manirathnam, who has now joined the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest in Delhi, says her fight was deeply personal.

He says Anitha was raised by their father, a daily wage labourer, after their mother died when she was seven. He recalls that Anitha wanted to become a doctor because their mother’s death due to an illness had shaped her dream of entering medicine.

“She wanted to become a doctor because she had seen the suffering caused by the lack of medical care,” Manirathnam said, recalling his sister’s journey.

Anitha joined the legal battle against NEET and became one of the petitioners before the Supreme Court, seeking relief for Tamil Nadu students. The Court did not grant the exemption sought by the state, and days later, on 1 September 2017, Anitha died by suicide at her home in Ariyalur.

Speaking about the impact of NEET on his family, Manirathnam said, “NEET has destroyed my family.”

Years later, he has joined the CJP protest, saying Tamil Nadu’s opposition to NEET began with students like Anitha, who questioned whether a single national entrance exam could account for the inequalities faced by students across the country. 

@hey_eshwar reports.
